Content:
Bit disappointed you didnt mention the Australian police in the intro. The the AN0M service was distributed by the FBI and the AFP....

The domain seizure notices placed on the AN0M website had the header with the FBIs logo, and the AFPs logo.

The AFP set up the first iBot server in Australia. 

e.g. "Before the devices were put to use, however, the FBI, and the AFP had a backdoor built into the communication platform which allowed law enforcement agencies to decrypt and store the messages as the messages were transmitted. "

Im not saying Europol and other nations didn't contribute. But this was originally a joint operation between the US and Australia.

Content:
The thing that is interesting to me in this whole situation, is the idea of privacy. On one hand, yeah there are for sure cases where it might be uncomfortable and awkward for people to know what you're doing, that's completely true, and for some people's safety, privacy can be very important. However, this being said, where there is privacy there is room for the more dark things to exist, so how much freedom, and how much privacy, can we really afford? More freedom turns to a multifaceted issue, it could make people feel like they can do whatever they want, even bad, it can make people more self-centered because who is going to stop or judge them? Etc. As I also already stated, privacy can let evil things slip mostly unchecked and unnoticed. 

Ultimately this entire case, I feel, highlights the complex tug of war, that is many of the rights and morals and ethics that exist now then and in time to come. It is essentially a very confusing topic indeed.

Content:
3:30 I might be either very st*pid or a genius, but my idea was to put these phones in Faraday cages as soon as you get them, so before whatever company is alerted to delete the data.
These commands do not work magically. Someone has to send the delete command, which I assume work even if the phone is off.
So just put the phone in a place in which the very signal is blocked.
Now that would probably lead in the future to some sort of internal kill switch, in which by either time or by the fact that you cannot relay a message, that would automatically delete the data. For example, the phone constantly pings some place, and if that ping stops for 10 minutes, then the phone automatically deletes the data.
But imagine going through a tunnel as a war lord and suddenly on the other side of the tunnel you have lost all your data.
In other words, there is a limit to how much you can fine tune these things and make them still usable for most people.
Anyway, putting them in a Faraday cage as you grab them still gives you a better chance than not doing it. Then you just move to a human size Faraday cage and you work on the phone there.
